# data/

## Committed

**`golden_eval_set.json`** — the evaluation dataset. 60 cases authored against the five
governed YAML skill files in the repository root. This is the measuring instrument and is
version-controlled deliberately: a quality number is only interpretable alongside the
cases it was computed over.

## Generated by `eval_runner.py`

None of the following is committed with meaningful content, because none of it can be
authored honestly — each file is the output of a real pipeline execution.

| File | Written by | Contents |
|---|---|---|
| `model_responses.json` | `--all` / `--responses` | Generated responses for the most recent run |
| `judge_results.json` | `--all` / `--judge` | LLM-judge verdicts for the most recent run |
| `evaluation_runs.json` | every run | Run metadata, computed summaries, deterministic records |
| `runs/<run_id>/…` | every run | Frozen per-run copies, so earlier runs stay comparable |
| `human_annotations.json` | the Human Evaluation page, and `--all` | Human annotations plus regenerated demo-profile annotations |

To populate them:

```bash
export GROQ_API_KEY="..."
python eval_runner.py --all --label "current"
```

Until then, every page in the application renders an empty state naming what is missing.
No page displays a placeholder number.

## Annotation provenance

`human_annotations.json` mixes two record types and they are never conflated:

- `rater_type: "human"` — a person applied the rubric in the Human Evaluation page.
  Preserved across runs; `eval_runner.py` never overwrites these.
- `rater_type: "demo_profile"` — a scripted rubric profile (see `demo_raters.py`).
  **Not a human annotator.** Regenerated on every run, because these read the actual
  response text and must match the responses currently on disk.

Every agreement statistic in the application reports human-only, demo-only and combined
populations separately.
